newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Airlines posts second-quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Airlines posts second-quarter profit.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp. on Wednesday reported its first quarterly profit since narrowly averting financial failure late last year.

Canadian, a Calgary-based national airline one-third owned by AMR Corp.'s American Airlines unit, earned a net profit of C$2.6 million ($1.9 million), or C38 cents (28 cents) a share, in the second quarter, versus a year-earlier net loss of C$23.8 million ($17.4 million), or C43 cents (31 cents) a share.
Quarterly revenues fell to C$770.8 million ($563 million) from C$786.9 million ($574 million) last year.
Canadian Airlines stock rose C37 cents to C$3.27 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on almost 625,000 shares, eclipsing its 52-week high of C$3.10. The stock's 52-week low was C$1.05.

It was the airline's first quarterly profit since the third quarter of 1996, when it earned C$86 million ($63 million), or C$1.11 ($0.81) a share. The carrier has not earned an annual profit in this decade.
Late last year, Canadian teetered on the brink of financial collapse before initiating a controversial restructuring plan in which it lowered costs and realigned its route network.

Canadian said its second-quarter operating profit of C$25.6 million ($19 million), versus an operating loss of C$1.7 million ($1.2 million) in the year-earlier quarter, reflected benefits from the restructuring.

"While we enjoyed the full benefits of the cost reductions during the second quarter, the network realignment was only completed in May and its benefit is just beginning to be realised," Chief Executive Kevin Benson said in a statement.

Canadian initiated the restructuring late last year after a succession of heavy annual losses and losing market share to rival Air Canada. The plan included reductions in employee wages, fuel taxes, overhead costs and service fees payable to American.

The airline said it also benefited in the latest quarter from fuel excise tax rebates received from the Canadian and British Columbia governments and a reduction of aviation fuel tax payable to Alberta.
